question: The term 'geography' was coined by who among the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eratosthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eratosthenes was a Greek mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, and music theorist.
 
• He is best known for being the first person to use the term 'geography' and for his work in geography, particularly his calculation of the Earth's circumference.
 
• He was the chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.
 
• Eratosthenes created one of the earliest maps of the world and introduced the concept of latitude and longitude.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eratosthenes' Contributions to Geography**

 
 
• Eratosthenes is often referred to as the 'Father of Geography' for his significant contributions to the field.
 
• He invented the discipline of geography, including the terminology we still use today.
 
• One of his most famous achievements was calculating the circumference of the Earth with remarkable accuracy for his time.
 
• He also created a system of latitude and longitude, which laid the foundation for modern cartography and navigation.
 
 
 
• **Al Idrisi**
 
 
• Al Idrisi was an Arab Muslim geographer, cartographer, and Egyptologist who lived in the 12th century.
 
• He is best known for his work "Tabula Rogeriana," which is one of the most advanced medieval world maps.
 
• His work was highly influential in the medieval Islamic world and in Europe.
 
 
 
• **Ptolemy**
 
 
• Ptolemy was a Greco-Egyptian writer of Alexandria, known for his work in astronomy, mathematics, and geography.
 
• He authored the "Geographia," a comprehensive treatise on the geographical knowledge of the Greco-Roman world.
 
• Ptolemy's work influenced geographic thought for over a thousand years.
 
 
 
• **Carl Ritter**
 
 
• Carl Ritter was a German geographer who is considered one of the founders of modern geography.
 
• He emphasized the importance of empirical observation and the interrelation between human and physical geography.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for future geographical studies and education.
